segments.name: North America – General Tool
segments.description: Rents general construction and industrial equipment to construction, industrial and do-it-yourself customers across the United States and Canada.
segments.evidence: The North America – General Tool segment provides flexible rental solutions designed to meet broad, general-purpose job site needs, such as mobile elevating work platforms, skid steers, excavators, lighting equipment and small general tools.

segments.name: North America – Specialty
segments.description: Provides specialized, technically demanding rental products with low rental penetration to predominantly non-construction customers in the United States and Canada.
segments.evidence: This segment includes products that require specialized knowledge and technical capabilities to operate and maintain, such as products relating to power & HVAC, climate control, scaffolding, film & TV equipment, flooring solutions, pump solutions, industrial tool, trench safety, ground protection, temporary structures, and temporary fencing.

segments.name: United Kingdom
segments.description: Rents General Tool and Specialty equipment through a regional store network to construction, industrial, infrastructure and energy customers in the United Kingdom.
segments.evidence: United Kingdom, which delivers a comprehensive range of General Tool and Specialty products and services to customers primarily located across the United Kingdom.

revenueModel.text: Customers, from multinational businesses to local contractors and do-it-yourselfers, pay to rent construction, industrial and specialty equipment by period.
revenueModel.evidence: Our customers range in size and scale from multinational businesses, to well-established local contractors and individual do-it-yourselfers, and include construction and industrial customers

changes.text: In fiscal 2026 the United Kingdom segment underwent an operational restructure that triggered an interim goodwill impairment test.
changes.evidence: During the fiscal year ended April 30, 2026, an impairment indicator was identified in the U.K. reporting unit as a result of the operational restructure of the United Kingdom segment.
